answers.text: Agreed, and drafted as you asked. The proposed draft's figurative phrases were these: "that rule has no brake", "asking for a hand in marriage", "leaves only one clean state", "whose final destination", and "nihilism wearing a kindly mask". Each is now literal (no limiting principle; proposing marriage; leaves only one final condition; whose logical conclusion; and nihilism disguised as humanitarian concern, which is your own phrase). The proposal had also dropped words with specific meaning; they are restored: subordinate consideration, supreme definition of the good, objective examination, emotional distress, illness, and anti-natalism as the highest environmental and moral virtue. The three-item list stays a list, because the passage already uses one. New item: call:civ/chapters/06_ch06.md:b8e79ee3:note/literal-wording. If you accept it, this held item can be withdrawn.

Read as a paragraph move, and drafted with your original wording. The last sentence ("A society where strangers extend dispositional love...") joins the paragraph that gives the reasons (cheap, non-rivalrous, orderly), and the next paragraph then opens "For those reasons, dispositional love is the proper default..." in the plural. The cadence draft itself was not carried over: its close ("A town of barred doors spends its strength on locks") is a metaphor, and it replaced swindler, criminal, or enemy with cheat, thief, or foe. New item: call:civ/chapters/08_ch08.md:8e3dbdb8:note/paragraph-move.

Drafted in three parts. (1) The rhetorical question now states the problem first; your two mechanisms and the bold phrase are unchanged. (2) Examples follow, each checked against the primary document. Verification: the Department for Work and Pensions' own account (face-to-face checks unavailable in 2020; estimated fraud of 6.3 billion pounds, up from 2.8 billion; fraud advertised on social media once the checks were eased), the National Audit Office (controls suspended; Universal Credit overpayments from 9.4 to 14.7 percent), and the California State Auditor (10.4 billion dollars of 111 billion paid on claims that could be fraudulent, 810 million of it to claimants whose records matched prisoners). Duration: a thirteen-week United States program of 2008 amended eleven times and paid to 2013, and a food benefit that ran from 2020 to 2023 and was followed by a permanent summer program from 2024. Order: the House of Commons committee on the August 2011 disorder, which found the disorder spread on the perception that police "had lost control of the streets", and that some joined because they saw the police "standing by and not arresting anyone". (3) The closing paragraph keeps your two sentences and adds the idea they generalize: kindness restrains abuse only where the giver knows the receiver, so an agency can give strangers only a fixed rule applied alike, which is politeness. Two cautions are written into the draft: legislators, not claimants, made the temporary provisions lasting; and the 2011 committee found officers too few and too slow, not an order to stand down. Seattle's occupied zone of 2020 was examined and left out: the review panel felt that the decision to withdraw from the East Precinct defused the tension at the barricades, and the police chief described reports of extortion there as rumors, no police report of it having been filed. New item: call:civ/chapters/08_ch08.md:9547789f:note/examples-and-rule.

The proposal is easier to read because it trims exactly what carries the accuracy. Four losses: "roughly eighty to a hundred years" became "within a hundred years"; "administering the courts" became "judging in the courts"; "inanimate storage media" became "saved on paper"; and the birth sentence lost "across the population as a whole" and "healthy, well-formed families", and turned replacement into "hold its ground". It also ends on a figure ("Civilization lives only in living hands"). Drafted in two alternates. a: your text with each of the three facts ended at its colon, so that no sentence carries a second claim; every word kept. b: the same, plus the library sentence put into a forward order; every term kept. The sentence listing who will be dead is left alone: its weight is your four roles, which cannot be moved forward without moving or shortening them. New item: call:civ/chapters/10_ch10.md:1804f760:note/keep-quantifiers.

Research done, and a new opening drafted from sources, in two alternates. First, what the record will and will not support in your list. (1) Ancient Greece: Polybius, Histories 37.9, in his own time after 146 BCE, on a low birth rate and a falling population in all Greece without war or plague, which he blames on men who would not marry or would rear one or two children. Aristotle on Sparta's citizens falling below a thousand is in the record, but he blames the laws of inheritance and the concentration of land, and notes that Sparta rewarded large families, so Sparta is not used as a case of refusing children. (2) The area in Eastern Europe: the Ormánság, a region of south-western Hungary where families kept to one child from the late eighteenth century, at first to keep their land undivided. The region lost people. In the seven villages studied together, the population rose by five percent between 1870 and 1941 while the population of Hungary rose from 188 to 350 on the same index (1785 = 100), and six of the seven shrank; Besence fell from above three hundred early in the nineteenth century to under two hundred by 1970 (Szántó, 2015; Koloh, 2021, in Bagdi's review, 2023; Andorka, 1970). The Hungarian statistical office gives the result per generation: from 100 people, 40 in the next generation, then 16, then 6.4. (3) Quakers: the chapter's existing case is the Shakers, not the Quakers (section 3, on the Shakers' rule of celibacy); I assumed you meant that passage and left it where it is. (4) Rome, two elements. Augustus, in Suetonius, on why he could not withdraw the grain distributions: they would one day be renewed through desire for popular favour. And the currency: the denarius was pure silver under Augustus and about four-fifths silver after Nero's reform of 64 (one re-analysis; the older figure is about nine-tenths), below half by the Severans; the antoninianus, introduced in 214, was below five percent silver in its last issues before 270; and wheat in Egypt stood at three drachmae the artaba under Augustus and two hundred in 276. The opening uses the first; the second is in the research report if you want it in section 5. (5) Zimbabwe after 2000 and South Africa: both verified from official documents and used. Rhodesia-era facts were not researched, so nothing compares the two periods. (6) The island's mine and endowment is Nauru, already in Chapter 10, so the draft points to it instead of repeating it. (7) People's ideas of why they decline: four are quoted in the draft, oldest first, Sallust (after Carthage fell, leisure and wealth became a burden and a curse), Ibn Khaldun (a dynasty does not as a rule outlast three generations), Gibbon (immoderate greatness), and Mancur Olson (stable societies accumulate organizations for collective action). Olson's sentences were checked against a working paper that quotes his chapter 3, not against the book itself. Also verified and not used: Glubb's stages and 250 years (an essay; no scholarly test found), Tainter on the declining returns of complexity, and Toynbee's creative minority that becomes a dominant minority. The draft's shape: the four writers; then four records (the grain distribution; the one-child custom; Zimbabwe, with Nauru pointed to; state capture and power rationing in South Africa); then your three closing paragraphs and your list, unchanged, and your thesis sentence kept word for word. Alternate a has all four records (969 words against 258); alternate b keeps the first two (732 words). Each record can be dropped without breaking the argument. Two of your mechanisms, the Compassionate Delusion and fatalism, have no case in the record I verified, and the draft does not pretend otherwise. One figure left out on purpose: Zimbabwe's tobacco crop is given as about 237 million kilograms in 2000 by the Tobacco Industry and Marketing Board, but I could not open that document directly, so the draft gives only the 2008 low and the 2018 recovery, which I read in a saved paper. New item: call:civ/chapters/11_ch11.md:056cf91e:note/opening-from-cases.

Done as you directed: your wording, cut to able-bodied adults. The corporate sentences are removed from the paragraph and from its Defense line. One consequence for you to decide: nothing in the chapter now treats corporate rent-seeking on its own. If you want it kept as a separate subsection, say so and it will be drafted from sources. New item: call:civ/chapters/11_ch11.md:ec330947:note/individuals-only.

Your text is untouched. One paragraph is added after the fourth stage, for the failure that needs no activist: the conscientious man silences himself because he wishes to be kind and takes every unkind act for a wrong one. Failing the student who did not study, dismissing the employee who will not work, and refusing further help to the repeat offender are unkind in the plain sense of the word, and a society requires them, because a boundary that no one will enforce against the person who violates it is not a boundary. The Marcuse section later in the chapter already says that the advocate of compassion over rules is often no strategist; the new paragraph puts that point where the five stages are. New item: call:civ/chapters/11_ch11.md:eb88fba0:note/own-unkindness.

Both instructions carried out: Hegel now "replaced correspondence truth with" (the word "fixed" is gone), and the Marx sentences are your original, verbatim, given a paragraph of their own. The rest of the proposal was not carried over, because it exchanged terms of art: trained for cultivated, middle tiers for mediating tiers, the state for the unitary state, equal law for symmetrical law, class purge for class liquidation, private plots and shops for private property, words never touch the world for language never refers to objective reality, tools of rule for instruments of power, and police states and starved land for tyranny and famine. What the draft takes from the proposal is its plainer first sentence and three splits that cost no term (Hegel's last sentence; the Rawls sentence; Rawls and Foucault in separate paragraphs). New item: call:civ/chapters/12_ch12.md:37f6e171:note/terms-restored. If you did want any of those substitutions, name it and it will go in.

Streamlined by structure only; every phrase of specific meaning is kept. Changes: one filler sentence removed ("The direct meaning of that statement is unmistakable."); the farmer contrast stated as rule first and case second; the proverb and the outcome-egalitarianism parallel each beginning a new sentence instead of following a colon; the Dasein sentence split after "the only real actor"; and the Land Power sentence split before its consequence. The proposal's replacements were not carried over: anti-Western right (for anti-Western, anti-procedural right), universal truth and fixed truth (for correspondence truth), Atlanticist habit (for Atlanticist / Anglo-Saxon episteme), self-anchored home (for self-anchored household), Eurasian Land Power and Western Sea Power without your parentheticals, and equal law (for procedural symmetry). New item: call:civ/chapters/12_ch12.md:3da9c1ce:note/streamline-keep-terms.

Drafted without adding a paragraph. The sentence that announced "an objective standard" is replaced by one that says what kind of test the five questions are: "It provides one test of compatibility for judging history, philosophy, religion, and politics. Two compatible doctrines can still be at odds, but a doctrine that fails is self-defeating or an enemy within." The five questions are your original text, not the proposal's, which had rewritten the fourth and fifth. "Neo-feudal warlordism" is dropped from the next paragraph: note 24 found that it is not Haywood's program and cut it from section 3A, but it had remained here. Length: 272 to 288 words. New item: call:civ/chapters/12_ch12.md:98535b9f:note/compatibility-test. One question for you: should the two verdicts be defined there (self-defeating when its program destroys its own people, Principle 3; enemy within when it sets its law above the common law, Principles 1 and 5)? I left them undefined to hold the length.

The study figure is gone. The facts come from Hume's own account (My Own Life, 1776): the librarianship paid him "little or no emolument"; the copy money for the History made him "not only independent, but opulent"; Political Discourses (1752) was the one work of his that succeeded on first publication. The draft: he earned his living by writing; the History of England (1754 to 1761) sold so well that he became, in his own words, "not only independent, but opulent"; in that history and in the Political Discourses he showed that he understood property, contract, and the danger of political fanaticism; then your sentence on his philosophy, unchanged. One point to check: Hume says he gave the last volumes to the public in 1761; their title pages are dated 1762, which is the date the Stanford Encyclopedia and the Hume Society use. I followed Hume. New item: call:civ/chapters/12_ch12.md:c60e0f50:note/direct-language.

Terms kept, and the reasonable edits applied. Not carried over: human differences (for human particularity), train strong character and high skill (for cultivating high character and technical excellence), drew an image from ironwork (for compared civic character to metallurgy), every mind is alike (for the reality of human cognitive and executive variation), pull down (for persecutes, drives out, or levels down), strict schools (for rigorously meritocratic schools), a dockworker's son (for the son of a manual laborer), and pulls the whole nation up (a figure). Carried over as structure: the opening phrase becomes its own sentence, the ninety percent sentence is split, and the scholarship sentence is split in two. No word of substance changes. New item: call:civ/chapters/13_ch13.md:3cf06304:note/keep-terms.

Research done twice; the second draft replaces the first under the same item (call:civ/chapters/13_ch13.md:14d51098:note/red-green-sourced). The first answer, filed earlier today, replaced your five mechanics with four signs of its own. That was the wrong shape. The new draft keeps your five points, by name and in order, and gives each a finding on record with its limit. Your working notes of 16 July 2026 supplied the model the five points stand for: book1-5/notes/red_green_alliance.md (identical copy at book1-6/sources/notes/), with the section "When opposing systems coordinate" in book1-6/chapters/2600_packages_purity.md. Tendencies and mechanisms, persons and not packages, illustrations and not proof: the draft is written to that register. What the record supports: the pairing appears in separate, dated instances (the Stop the War Coalition, the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament and the Muslim Association of Britain co-organizing the London demonstration of 15 February 2003; Ken Livingstone's welcome for Yusuf al-Qaradawi in 2004, with his own words that he did not agree with Qaradawi "on lesbian and gay rights"; the Paris march of 10 November 2019, initiated with the CCIF and signed by the leaders of the CGT, Europe Écologie Les Verts, Générations and the Communist Party and by every deputy of Jean-Luc Mélenchon's party). The CCIF was dissolved in December 2020, and the Conseil d'État upheld the dissolution in September 2021 on the ground of provocation to hatred while rejecting the terrorism ground. What the record does not support, as the section was written: one coordinated alliance; a left-Islamist highway blockade, or the motive of demonstrating police timidity; and entry through diversity-and-inclusion mandates. The closing prognosis and its three bullets are removed, as you directed. Three corrections to my own earlier answer and draft: (1) a police crowd figure of 10,500 that I gave beside the 13,500 had no source in the record, and is removed; (2) the file I had saved of the Secretary of State's speech at Istanbul on 15 July 2011 was an error page; the speech is now saved from the Internet Archive, and it does say that the resolution calls on states to protect freedom of religion "but not to criminalize speech unless there is an incitement to imminent violence", so Resolution 16/18 should not be cited as a blasphemy instrument; (3) the Prevent review's sentence about advisory boards (para. 3.29) concerns the experts it consulted and is not evidence of entryism. Sources added today and saved under ext-ref/red_green: Peter Clarke's report on the Birmingham schools (HC 576, 2014) and three news reports of the labor board's memorandum on the Google dismissal; the memorandum itself could not be saved.

A structural diagnosis, and one draft. The defect as written: the tool is titled for the unfalsifiable argument, but the section defines only asymmetrical accounting, and only its sixth point concerns falsifiability; the six points are a list whose order is not stated; and the audit is never turned on the speaker's own doctrine. The draft (606 words against 423) makes three changes and keeps your six points word for word: a paragraph names both devices by which the claim survives (asymmetrical accounting, and the absence of any stated condition of failure) and defines unfalsifiable; each point ends with the evasion it closes, and point 2 refers to Tool 2; a closing paragraph applies the audit to one's own doctrine under Principle 5. "Self-sealing" is removed as a figure. The Venezuela example stays the hypothetical it is. If by "larger than rephrasing" you meant replacing it with a sourced case (the fall of Venezuelan oil output and the sanctions timeline, with the defenders' actual explanations), that is a research task not yet begun; say so and it will be done. New item: call:civ/chapters/14_ch14.md:a69db048:note/tool1-rework.

Rebuilt on your test. The old rule asked only whether the doctrine's text forbade the act. The draft starts with the doctrine's scope. A doctrine that prescribes a political and social order is tested by its program: rulers who carry out what its texts instruct are the doctrine's record, and the sentences on Lenin, Stalin, Mao, and Pol Pot are yours, verbatim. An ethic that explicitly leaves politics to another authority has no program: the Gospels are quoted in the NET wording chapter 12 uses ("give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's", Matthew 22:21; "My kingdom is not from this world", John 18:36), and the question becomes whether the political act was a direct result of the doctrine. It was, if the texts command it or if rules that the doctrine's own recognized authorities derive from them command it. It was not, if no text commands it and the texts forbid it. The judge example is kept as the simplest case, with its citations made exact. The old sentence said that Article II, the bribery statutes, and the judicial oath "explicitly forbid accepting bribes in explicit statutory text", which is true of none of them in that form: Article II, Section 4 makes bribery a ground for removal from office, 18 U.S.C. § 201 makes it a crime, and the oath binds the judge to administer justice without respect to persons (28 U.S.C. § 453). A last sentence applies the test alike to the accuser's own doctrine. Two things left for you: whether Islam should be named as a doctrine of the first kind, since chapter 12 treats its law as a political order; and whether the Inquisition should be judged outright in the text, or left to the reader who applies the test. New item: call:civ/chapters/14_ch14.md:f1c85c31:note/tool2-rework.
